items.title: Makafui Woanyah retains NPP Volta Regional Chairmanship
items.description: Makafui Kofi Woanyah has secured another term as the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Volta Regional Chairman after winning the party’s regional executive elections. Mr Woanyah defeated his challenger, Joseph Wallace Homenya, by 21 votes in the contest. Provisional results indicate that the incumbent polled 169 votes, compared with 148 votes for Mr Homenya. The election had generated interest within the party, with supporters of Mr Woanyah pointing to his role in the development of the NPP’s structures and its electoral activities in the Volta Region as reasons for his victory. His opponent, however, attracted support from members who believed the party required a change in leadership and a different strategy to rebuild its support base. They argued that fresh leadership could help unite the party, improve its appeal and attract more members ahead of future elections. Mr Woanyah’s victory means he will continue to oversee the NPP’s affairs in the Volta Region as the party works to reorganise its structures and improve its electoral fortunes.

items.title: Ghana Law Society announces maiden annual Bar conference for September 30
items.description: The Ghana Law Society (GLS) has announced its maiden Annual Bar Conference, scheduled to take place on Wednesday, September 30, as part of efforts to promote dialogue and strengthen the legal profession in Ghana. The conference will be held under the theme, “Legal Reforms: The Place of the Ghanaian Lawyer”, with the venue to be announced later. In a statement issued on behalf of the National Executive Council of the GLS on Saturday, August 15, the General Secretary, Sam Atukwei Quaye, said the conference would bring together key stakeholders from Ghana’s legal profession and beyond. “This landmark event will bring together legal practitioners, judges, policymakers, corporate leaders, and distinguished guests from across Ghana and beyond,” the statement said. President John Dramani Mahama is expected to attend the conference as the Special Guest of Honour. Other speakers expected to participate include the Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin; Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie; Attorney General and Minister of Justice, Dominic Akuritinga Ayine; President of the Law Society of Kenya, Charles Kanjama; and legal scholar Professor Patrick Lumumba. The GLS said the conference forms part of its commitment to strengthening the practice of law and creating a platform for engagement among legal practitioners, government, other actors within the legal profession and the wider public. The society said the event would provide an opportunity for participants to discuss legal reforms and examine the role of Ghanaian lawyers in shaping the country’s justice system and broader governance. Registration for the conference is open through the GLS conference portal. The society has set different registration fees based on the number of years a lawyer has been at the Bar. Lawyers who have been called to the Bar for between zero and four years will pay GH¢500, while those with five to nine years at the Bar will pay GH¢1,000. Lawyers with 10 years or more at the Bar will pay GH¢1,500. Law students who are members of the GLS will pay GH¢100, while non-member law students will pay GH¢150. The GLS said the fees are all-inclusive and encouraged lawyers and law students to register and participate in the conference. GLS Annual Bar Conf. Press Release pdf Download

items.title: Osun Election: Let the people’s will prevail, INEC must uphold integrity — Adeleke
items.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to uphold the highest standards of integrity in the collation of results from Saturday’s governorship election, saying the will of the people must prevail. Adeleke made the call in a post on his X handle on Saturday as the election moved into the results collation stage. The governor commended the people of Osun State for turning out in large numbers to participate in the election. “Against all odds, the people of Osun State have turned out in large numbers and are speaking with one voice,” he said. Adeleke also commended security agencies deployed for the election, urging them to remain vigilant as results are collated from polling units to wards and local government areas. “The safety and protection of our people is paramount. I commend the security agencies deployed for this election and urge them to remain vigilant as we move into the collation of results; from polling units to wards to local government areas. “I also call on INEC to uphold the highest standards of integrity throughout this process,” he said. The governor expressed confidence in the professionalism of the institutions involved in the election, saying the Federal Government had provided adequate security for the exercise. He stressed that democracy was strongest when the wishes of voters were respected and the sanctity of their votes protected. “Democracy is at its strongest when we honour the wishes of our people and protect the sanctity of their votes,” Adeleke said. He urged Osun residents to remain peaceful, law-abiding and committed to the democratic process. “To every Osun citizen: I urge you to remain peaceful, law-abiding, and committed to this democratic moment. “Let the people’s will prevail,” he added. items.title: The Truths That Failed Jason Arday
items.description: Yesterday in London, Jason Arday, the controversy-plagued British academic and author, was found dead. Made famous as the youngest Black professor in Cambridge’s more than 800-year history, Arday had been dogged by weeks of scrutiny amid accusations of plagiarism, fake qualifications, and a fabricated backstory filled with hard-to-believe details. He claimed to have been mute until age 11 and illiterate until 18, disadvantages that did not deter him from getting a Ph.D., which he earned by age 30. He claimed, too, that he had suffered from various medical conditions throughout his life, including autism, epilepsy, locked-in syndrome, testicular cancer, and a brain tumor. He was, by his account, a world-class endurance athlete who had racked up a variety of impressive feats, including running 600 miles in six days. Then there were his academic accomplishments: Arday was billed as a once-in-a-generation talent, whose research in his field—the sociology of education—was “the best in the world,” according to Hilary Cremin, the head of Cambridge’s faculty of education. He claimed to have received a book advance of 1.4 million in unspecified currency for his memoir, released this week by Simon & Schuster. It was a meteoric rise, until it wasn’t. Last month, Nathan Cofnas—a former Cambridge researcher who may politely be described as a philosopher with a special interest in race and IQ, and who may impolitely be described as a professional racist—published in his newsletter what appeared to be significant evidence of Arday’s plagiarism. This month, as it became apparent that much of the Arday legend was most likely just that, the academic became an object of international obsession, especially in British media and on X. He resigned from Cambridge last week, though this did not stem the flood of attention. The online hive mind, in particular, was brutal until the moment of Arday’s death, at which point the collective swarm did an about-face. The same platform that loosed an algorithmically accelerated torrent of abuse is now dominated by kind remembrances and mawkishness. I find the whole pageantry grotesque. What I propose is that the public give Arday a courtesy in death that he was often denied in life: Let’s treat him like a person. Not like Cambridge’s magical negro, or like Simon & Schuster’s golden goose, or like the fetish object of internet racists, but like a flawed human being who should still be alive but is not. That requires being honest about who Arday was, not despite his tragic death but because of it. After all, it was systemic, ritualized dishonesty—his own and others’—that undid him. [ Read: Icarus in the faculty lounge ] Here is the truth about Jason Arday: A preponderance of evidence suggests that he was a serial fabulist and unrepentant plagiarist who successfully conned a British academic aristocracy so blinded by do-gooder racial neurosis that it was unable to spot lies that would have been obvious to any Joe Schmo. (Arday denied intentional misconduct and suggested that his apparent plagiarism was a result of his autism, which he said meant that he tended to learn through imitation.) As evidence of those seeming lies mounted, the powerful institutions that had made him continued to back him, doubling down and raising the stakes. Simon & Schuster stood by its author—or perhaps more accurately, stood by its product. Even as the evidence of fraud became all but undeniable, the publisher did not merely declare that it would press forward with Arday’s book; it had the audacity to tout “the professionalism and integrity he has brought to every stage of the publication.” Then those on the racist right—frothing with glee that they took no trouble to conceal—pressed their advantage, punch-drunk on the double intoxicant of incandescent liberal hypocrisy and a Black man’s failure. The mob swelled, online and in the media. Some people joined out of perfectly legitimate indignation at the apparent obliteration of academic standards that the ordeal attested to. Some joined out of ghoulish pleasure at seeing a beneficiary of DEI, as they cast him, cut down to size. Everyone following this story would do well to engage in some reflection. I will confess that, until yesterday, I had watched the Arday saga unfold with some combination of amusement and distress. Amusement because of the undeniable comic absurdity to the revelation that the best and brightest minds at Cambridge had been so easily deceived by a man who claimed to have run nine marathons in about as many days on a fractured fibula, and who maintained that his future had been predicted by a Brazilian shaman. Distress because I could relate to some of the things that Arday might have experienced. [ From the September 2026 issue: Why I quit the tenure track ] I have written, in this magazine and elsewhere, about what it is like to be the beneficiary of affirmative action in elite spaces. I have seen, firsthand, the way a specific kind of white progressive treats Black men who have overcome obstacles. They cannot conceal a certain blend of of pity and glee when they learn, for example, that my biological father left before I was old enough to walk, or that I was raised for a time by a single mother. It is a look that says, How far you’ve come, and how kind I am for helping you go further . I have always found such encounters stomach-churning. But I can also imagine—if you came up hard and are unaccustomed to kindness—how good it might feel, and how tempting it might be, to do and say things that make people give you that look again and again, whether or not the things you’re saying are strictly true. Two images have rattled around in my head since the news of Arday’s death. The first is from a 2023 BBC clip celebrating his hiring at Cambridge. Cremin, Arday’s Cambridge colleague, clasps both of his hands in the manner of a cherished loved one as they stare into each other’s eyes. The camera zooms in on their white and Black hands interlocked and lingers there. The second image was posted on X last night: a screenshot of a list of article headlines about the Arday scandal, stretching to several pages, published by one British outlet alone. It represents but a few watts of the international spotlight that had been trained on the academic. I have been dwelling on these two images—the theatrical interracial handclasp; the pages and pages of monomaniacal media coverage of what was ultimately a niche academic scandal—because together they speak to a terrible reality. Arday was fetishized in his ascendancy by white liberals, for whom he served as a mirror in which they could see their own goodness. And he was fetishized in his downfall by white conservatives who saw him as a test case for their own obsessions with an academic apparatus that they believe is not meritocratic enough—which is to say, not white enough. The right would have us believe that the Arday scandal is a story of affirmative action taken to its most caricaturish conclusion. Many progressives see it as something else: a racist witch hunt in which self-righteous zealots with suspect motives hounded a man to death. The problem with these narratives—and it is a sticky problem—is that they are both right. To be a Black person in elite institutions, and particularly in elite academia, is to have the standards simultaneously set too low and too high: too low because only a Black person with Arday’s dubious qualifications and seemingly invented biography could have been elevated to the top of the mountain in academia and publishing; and too high because only a Black person could have been pushed off that mountain with such nakedly racist enthusiasm, his tumbling fall so ruthlessly documented, analyzed, and cheered. When a famous white man errs, people tend to rightly understand his mistakes or transgressions as an individual’s missteps. When a famous Black man does, the errors are typically turned into spectacle, characterized as proof of the inferiority, suspected all along, of his race. Around the same time yesterday afternoon that I learned of Arday’s fate, I came across another piece of news: an announcement that Ross Barkan, a white novelist and journalist, had just been dropped by New York magazine after the publication—having investigated allegations regarding dozens of instances of plagiarism in Barkan’s writing—concluded that his work “did not live up to our editorial standards.” Swiftly afterward, Barkan announced that he would now focus on writing a new column at The Nation , another venerable outlet, where he will get a very public second chance. It is impossible to know what is in someone’s head or heart in their final moments. I have to imagine, though, that Arday understood well enough the world he had entered and how its rules tend to work: When you are Black, some people will open the door for you far wider than they should. And when that door abruptly comes swinging shut, you will be offered no second chances.

items.title: Rapport de l’IGE: des irrégularités s’élevant à deux milliards d’ouguias et le licenciement de 20 employés
items.description: L'Inspection générale de l'État a mis au jour des irrégularités ayant un impact financier supérieur à 2,37 milliards d'ouguiyas lors de ses missions de contrôle en 2024 et 2025, sur un montant total de 32,86 milliards d'ouguiyas ayant fait l'objet d'un audit, tandis que des mesures préventives d’un montant de 1,29 milliard d’ouguiyas ont été prises, que 524,48 millions d’ouguiyas ont été recouvrés ou font l’objet d’une procédure de recouvrement, et que des dossiers représentant un impact financier de 1,21 milliard d’ouguiyas ont été transmis aux autorités judiciaires, avec le licenciement de 20 agents et la prise d’autres mesures administratives et disciplinaires. Dans son rapport annuel d’activités, l’Inspection générale a indiqué avoir lancé 35 missions de contrôle, dont 28 missions programmées, cinq missions sur demande et deux missions de sa propre initiative. Parmi celles-ci, 28 ont été menées à bien, dont 11 en 2024 et 17 en 2025. Ces missions ont porté sur divers secteurs, notamment la protection sociale, l’emploi, les transports, les télécommunications, les infrastructures numériques, les minéraux, l’énergie, l’éducation, le logement et l’urbanisme, le développement de l’élevage, la santé, la pêche, les infrastructures maritimes et portuaires, ainsi que l’eau et l’assainissement. Le rapport a montré que les marchés publics constituaient le domaine le plus exposé aux irrégularités ayant un impact financier, représentant 60 % de cet impact, suivis par les irrégularités en matière de recouvrement des recettes et des créances (13 %), les obligations fiscales (8 %) et la gouvernance et le contrôle interne (6 %). Ces domaines représentent ensemble environ 87 % de l’impact financier des irrégularités constatées. Dans le cadre des mesures préventives, l’Inspection générale a indiqué avoir contribué à la rationalisation des dépenses publiques à hauteur de 603,76 millions d’ouguiyas et à la suspension de dépenses non justifiées d’un montant de 694,69 millions d’ouguiyas, l’impact financier total de ces mesures s’élevant à environ 1,29 milliard d’ouguiyas. Les montants recouvrés ou en cours de recouvrement se sont élevés à 524,48 millions d'ouguiyas, répartis entre 45,65 millions versés au Trésor public, 141,64 millions d'ouguiyas par recouvrement en nature et 139,77 millions par retenue sur les créances, tandis que les montants en cours de recouvrement s’élevaient à 197,41 millions d’ouguiyas. Sur le plan judiciaire, l’impact financier des dossiers transmis aux instances judiciaires compétentes s’est élevé à 1,21 milliard d’ouguiyas ; l’Inspection générale a transmis deux dossiers à la Cour des comptes et deux autres au parquet. Des mesures administratives et disciplinaires ont également été prises à l’encontre de fonctionnaires de différents échelons hiérarchiques, notamment le licenciement de 20 agents, ainsi que la mutation d’office et l’émission de 11 avertissements. Le rapport a recensé 771 recommandations visant à remédier aux irrégularités, dont 420 ont été mises en œuvre, tandis que 351 sont encore en cours de mise en œuvre ; quant aux mesures programmées, leur nombre s’élevait à 348, dont 231 ont été mises en œuvre.

items.description: Los incendios forestales han obligado a desalojar a más de 1.200 personas de sus viviendas entre Huesca y Zamora este sábado. El fuego de Las Peñas de Riglos (Huesca), el más preocupante de los dos, afecta ya a más de 16.600 hectáreas y mantiene fuera de sus casas a 1.045 personas. A los núcleos evacuados durante los últimos días se ha sumado esta tarde Bernués, con 25 habitantes, lo que eleva a 19 las poblaciones desalojadas. Mientras, un incendio declarado de madrugada en La Tejera, en el municipio zamorano de Hermisende, ha obligado a evacuar a unas 190 personas de Castromil y San Ciprián. Mientras, en Niebla (Huelva), el enorme fuego que ha recorrido más de 38.000 hectáreas ha dejado de avanzar por primera vez desde que comenzó hace ocho días. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Immersion patriotique obligatoire 2026 : Le Ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO appelle les nouveaux bacheliers de la région du Nakambé à incarner les valeurs du nouveau Burkinabè
items.description: Dans la matinée de ce samedi 15 août 2026, le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO, a rendu visite aux nouveaux bacheliers appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire 2026, dans la ville de Tenkodogo, région du Nakambé. Débutée le 27 juillet 2026 sur l’ensemble du territoire national, cette immersion vise notamment à renforcer chez les jeunes les valeurs de patriotisme, de courage, d’intégrité, de solidarité, de résilience et de combativité. Au cours de sa visite dans plusieurs établissements accueillant les appelés, notamment l’École privée de santé humaine Sainte-Jules, le Lycée privé Peng-Wendé de Tenkodogo, l’Institut de formation professionnelle et le lycée Rialé, le Ministre a transmis aux jeunes le message du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. S’adressant aux appelés, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO les a invités à faire de leur passage à l’immersion le point de départ d’une transformation personnelle et citoyenne. Il les a exhortés à adopter des comportements responsables, à cultiver l’intégrité et à se préparer à devenir les bâtisseurs du Burkina Faso de demain. Le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement a également insisté sur l’usage responsable des réseaux sociaux. Il a appelé les jeunes à se détourner des contenus sans valeur ou susceptibles de compromettre leur avenir et à privilégier les contenus éducatifs, constructifs et valorisant le savoir-faire burkinabè. Enfin, il les a exhortés à faire preuve de vigilance face aux fausses informations et aux contenus de désinformation diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux, en s’appuyant sur des sources médiatiques fiables. À travers cette immersion, le Gouvernement entend contribuer à la formation d’une jeunesse consciente, engagée et capable de défendre les intérêts du Burkina Faso. DCRP/MCCAT

items.title: Entre Fnideq et Sebta, une frontière sous étroite surveillance des deux côtés
items.description: Le calme régnait samedi matin au poste-frontière de Tarajal, principal point de passage vers la ville de Sebta occupée. Cette accalmie contraste avec l’important dispositif sécuritaire déployé de part et d’autre de la frontière, en réponse aux appels relayés sur les réseaux sociaux évoquant une possible tentative d’entrée massive de migrants le 15 août, selon des informations rapportées par Europa Press . Côté marocain, les autorités ont mis en place un dispositif d’une ampleur exceptionnelle afin d’empêcher tout afflux de candidats à la migration irrégulière. En mer, la Marine royale marocaine a mobilisé six embarcations semi-rigides chargées de surveiller le littoral. Sur terre, des milliers d’agents des Forces auxiliaires ont été déployés le long du périmètre frontalier, avec l’appui de gendarmes chargés notamment de sécuriser les zones montagneuses environnantes. Selon Europa Press , les mesures prises ne se limitent pas à la présence humaine. Le Maroc a également installé une nouvelle barrière métallique d’environ quatre mètres de hauteur à proximité de la frontière. Érigée au début de la semaine, cette structure longe la route reliant Fnideq au poste-frontière de Sebta. Son objectif est d’empêcher la formation de grands rassemblements de personnes dans les secteurs proches de la ligne de séparation. Le contrôle a par ailleurs été étendu au-delà du strict périmètre frontalier où des points de contrôle ont été mis en place à Fnideq. Un premier barrage de sécurité y a été installé afin de filtrer les déplacements vers la zone frontalière. La ville de Fnideq, jumelle de Sebta, « est sous le contrôle des militaires et des gendarmes », a affirmé à Europa Press un habitant de Sebta qui s’est récemment rendu au Maroc, témoignant de l’intensité du déploiement sécuritaire observé dans la région. L’Espagne renforce également sa présence Du côté espagnol, les autorités ont elles aussi renforcé leur dispositif depuis la soirée de vendredi. Le service maritime de la Garde civile patrouille en mer avec ses navires, tandis qu’à terre, des effectifs militaires et des agents de la Police nationale ont été mobilisés pour surveiller la frontière et prévenir toute tentative d’entrée irrégulière. Cette montée en puissance des moyens de sécurité intervient dans un contexte marqué par les événements survenus à la fin du mois de juillet. Lors d’une visite effectuée à Sebta mercredi dernier, la ministre espagnole de la Défense, Margarita Robles, a indiqué que quelque 80.000 personnes avaient franchi la frontière lors de l’afflux massif enregistré le 30 juillet. Les autorités des deux pays redoutent désormais qu’un nouvel épisode similaire puisse se produire à l’occasion du 15 août, date largement évoquée sur les réseaux sociaux ces derniers jours. Toutefois, les informations circulant en ligne ne permettent pas, à ce stade, de confirmer l’existence d’une nouvelle opération coordonnée ou d’une arrivée massive imminente. Malgré les rumeurs et les appels relayés sur différentes plateformes, la situation demeurait calme samedi à Tarajal. Les autorités marocaines et espagnoles maintiennent néanmoins leur vigilance, estimant que le contexte justifie le maintien d’un dispositif renforcé afin de prévenir tout mouvement de grande ampleur vers l’enclave espagnole, selon les informations relayées par Europa Press. Interpellation de 109 migrants subsahariens parmi 111 candidats à la migration irrégulière Par ailleurs, les autorités marocaines ont procédé , aux premières heures de la matinée du samedi 15 août, à l’interpellation de 111 candidats à la migration irrégulière à Fnideq et dans ses environs, dans le cadre d’opérations de contrôle et d’interventions de terrain destinées à prévenir toute tentative de franchissement illégal vers Sebta et Melilla, occupées. Selon une source sécuritaire, les personnes arrêtées comprennent 109 ressortissants d’Afrique subsaharienne ainsi que deux citoyens marocains. Ces opérations s’inscrivent dans un dispositif renforcé déployé par les autorités afin de contenir les mouvements migratoires irréguliers dans cette zone frontalière sensible du nord du Royaume. The post Entre Fnideq et Sebta, une frontière sous étroite surveillance des deux côtés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sécurité routière en Tunisie | Bilan alarmant de l’ATSR
items.description: ​La route continue de tuer à un rythme inquiétant en Tunisie, selon les dernières données communiquées par l'Association Tunisie pour la sécurité routière (ATSR). En effet, plus de 2820 accidents de la circulation ont été enregistrés depuis le début de l'année 2026 avec un bilan humain particulièrement lourd, déplorant déjà 810 décès et plus de 3700 blessés. Le gouvernorat de Kairouan se hisse au triste rang de la région la plus meurtrière du pays avec 67 personnes tuées, suivi de très près par le gouvernorat de Tunis, qui enregistre 64 décès. ​L'Association affirme que les facteurs humains demeurent la cause principale des tragédies, en citant l'excès de vitesse comme le facteur le plus mortel, directement impliqué dans 640 accidents ayant coûté la vie à 304 personnes. Parallèlement, le manque d'attention et la distraction au volant sont notés comme causes majeures de mortalité, responsables de 126 décès au cours de la même période. ​Face à ce constat alarmant, l'ATSR tire la sonnette d'alarme et souligne la nécessité absolue de multiplier les actions préventives et les contrôles, en particulier dans les gouvernorats les plus touchés, tout en réitérant son appel à l'ensemble des usagers à la vigilance, au respect des limitations de vitesse et à une conduite responsable. Y. N. L’article Sécurité routière en Tunisie | Bilan alarmant de l'ATSR est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

Chelsea fans boo Enzo Fernandez in friendly win over Sociedad
items.description: Enzo Fernandez was jeered by Chelsea supporters after coming on as a substitute during a 3-1 friendly win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Several fans made their feelings known when Fernandez, who has previously made clear his desire to leave Chelsea, came on in the 62nd minute to replace Reece James. But other supporters gave their backing to the 25-year-old Fernandez, who told the Blues in May he wanted to leave. Chelsea placed a reported asking price of £120 million ($162 million) on the Argentina international but no bids have yet been received during the summer transfer window. Fernandez scored Argentina’s equaliser in their World Cup semi-final win over England in July before being sent off in the South Americans’ defeat by Spain in the final. Record signing Morgan Rogers scored on his first Stamford Bridge appearance, tapping in the rebound after Joao Pedro’s header was saved. Brazilian Pedro ensured victory for new manager Xabi Alonso in the team’s final match before their Premier League opener away to local rivals Fulham, scoring a double to take his pre-season total to eight goals, after Jon Aramburu had equalised for the La Liga side. items.title: L’IGE au ministère de la santé : achat de médicaments dont la date de péremption est proche, matériel non réceptionné et un autre non entretenu
items.description: L'Inspection générale de l'État a constaté des irrégularités dans la gestion des médicaments et des équipements médicaux au sein du secteur de la santé, notamment l'acquisition de médicaments dont la date de péremption était proche, des problèmes de stockage et de gestion des stocks, ainsi que le paiement de sommes correspondant à des médicaments et équipements non réceptionnés, ainsi que la facturation de prestations de maintenance non effectuées. Ces constatations sont issues de deux missions de contrôle et d’audit menées au sein d’un secteur ministériel et d’un établissement public sur une période de six ans, entre 2019 et 2024, portant sur des montants contrôlés dépassant les 7,8 milliards d’ouguiyas. Les travaux de contrôle ont révélé, selon le rapport annuel de l’Inspection générale de l’État, des irrégularités financières, des ruptures d’approvisionnement et des dysfonctionnements dans les procédures d’acquisition de médicaments, notamment la conclusion de contrats de dépôt sur la base d’un paiement après-vente sans que les procédures d’évaluation et d’autorisation approuvées aient été respectées, ce qui a conduit à l’acquisition de médicaments dont la date de péremption était proche. Les inspections sur le terrain, menées avec la participation d’experts techniques, ont révélé la présence d’équipements médicaux inutilisés, d’autres inadaptés aux besoins réels ou non conformes aux normes techniques convenues, ainsi que l’absence de services de maintenance préventive et corrective pour certains équipements vitaux. Le rapport a également fait état d’une mauvaise gestion des stocks de médicaments et de matériel médical, notamment le stockage de quantités de médicaments périmés et l’accumulation de stocks de ceux-ci au fil des années, ainsi que des lacunes dans la planification et la coordination de l’acquisition des équipements et l’absence de registre ou de base de données des équipements médicaux. Selon le rapport, les irrégularités ayant une incidence financière comprenaient le détournement de fonds publics, une surfacturation, la facturation de services de maintenance non effectués, le versement de sommes pour des équipements et des médicaments non réceptionnés, la réception d’équipements non conformes aux spécifications, ainsi qu’un déficit dans la caisse de gestion des bons de carburant. L'Inspection a également constaté que des sommes dues avaient été versées avant le paiement des droits d'enregistrement, que les pénalités de retard n'avaient pas été prélevées ni recouvrées, ainsi que la prise en charge des frais d’eau et d’électricité pour des bâtiments qui ne sont plus loués, le non-recouvrement de sommes dues à l’État, sans compter des dépenses non étayées par des pièces justificatives suffisantes, et l’octroi de privilèges et de prêts à des employés sans garanties suffisantes pour leur recouvrement. Sur le plan administratif et en matière de marchés, le rapport a relevé des cas d’abus d’influence et d’abus de fonction pour l’attribution de marchés, le fractionnement des dépenses, une concurrence qualifiée de fictive, un recours injustifié à des accords directs et à des concessions illégales sur les marchés, ainsi que des contrats injustifiés avec des prestataires de services et des avances versées à des fournisseurs en violation des accords de paiement après-vente. L’Inspection a attribué une partie de ces dysfonctionnements à la faiblesse de la planification et de la programmation des besoins en médicaments et en équipements médicaux, à l’application insuffisante des règles de concurrence et de transparence, ainsi qu’à la faiblesse des mécanismes de suivi et de maintenance, estimant que cela avait eu un impact sur la continuité de l’approvisionnement en médicaments et en services de santé, ainsi que sur l’utilisation optimale des ressources publiques. Selon le rapport, les autorités compétentes ont pris des mesures comprenant la suspension du versement de paiements liés à des dépenses injustifiées, l’annulation d’un contrat conclu de gré à gré et sa remise en adjudication par le biais d’un appel d’offres ouvert, ce qui a permis de réaliser des économies considérables, sans compter la résiliation de contrats de location et de nettoyage injustifiés, la destruction des médicaments périmés et l’application de mesures administratives et disciplinaires. L’Inspection a recommandé de réparer les préjudices subis, de déterminer les besoins en médicaments, fournitures et équipements par le biais d’une planification participative, de réviser périodiquement les contrats de maintenance, la mise en place d’un système centralisé de gestion et de maintenance des équipements médicaux, l’amélioration des conditions de stockage des médicaments, la mise à jour de leurs autorisations de mise sur le marché, ainsi que la prise de mesures à l’encontre des entreprises en difficulté et la constitution d’équipes chargées du fonctionnement et de la maintenance des équipements médicaux.

items.title: NSMQ 2026: Check out the 147 schools battling in 49 preliminary contests
items.description: The 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) is set to begin its preliminary stage, with 147 schools preparing to battle for qualification to the next round of the prestigious academic competition. The national championship begins on Thursday, August 20, 2026, with the preliminary stage featuring 49 contests involving three schools in each contest. The preliminary stage marks the beginning of the journey towards the NSMQ national title, with participating schools expected to test their knowledge and speed across science and mathematics-related questions. For the contestants, however, the competition represents more than simply answering questions correctly. It is an opportunity to defend their schools’ reputations, build on past performances, and create a place for themselves in the history of Ghana’s academic competition. A total of 174 schools are expected to compete at the national championship stage this year. However, 27 schools have already secured automatic qualification to the One-Eighth Stage, leaving 147 schools to battle it out during the preliminary contests for the remaining qualification slots. items.title: Alerte pluie et canicule en Algérie : les régions concernées
items.description: Le mois d’août amorce sa deuxième quinzaine avec une double alerte à la pluie et à la canicule en Algérie. Lancée par l’Office national de la météorologie, une alerte pluie de niveau II (orange) concerne les wilayas de Mila, Constantine, Guelma, Souk Ahras, Oum El Bouaghi, Batna, Khenchela, Tébessa et Tamanrasset, de ce samedi à 14h00 jusqu’à demain, dimanche 16 août, à 02h00. Sur ces régions, il est attendu des précipitations comprises entre 20 et 40 mm. La wilaya de Tamanrasset a été touchée par des pluies diluviennes vendredi. La Protection civile a annoncé ce samedi avoir réussi à secourir trois personnes prises au pièges par les eaux de l’oued Tiglaline alors qu’elles étaient dans une voiture. A In M’guel, deux occupants d’un véhicule, qui était cerné par les eaux d’un oued en crue, ont été également sauvés par les pompiers. De la pluie et des températures élevées dans plusieurs régions d’Algérie À Oran, Ain Temouchent et Mostaganem, la pluie va tomber ce soir jusqu’à 01h00 du matin dimanche. De la pluie est annoncée aussi au niveau de plusieurs wilayas du pays ce soir. En plus de la pluie, l’Office national de la météorologie a lancé une alerte canicule demain, dimanche, dans les wilayas de Skikda, Annaba, El Tarf, Jijel, Bejaïa, Boumerdès, Tizi-Ouzou, Alger, Chlef, Mostaganem, Ain Temouchent et Tipaza. Cette vague de chaleur survient alors que les incendies continuent de ravager les forêts du pays. Le dernier point de situation publié par la Protection civile ce samedi à 07h00 faisait état de 27 incendies enregistrés, dont 26 ont été éteints, et un toujours en activité dans la wilaya de Jijel. items.title: Prospérité : ce que révèle le nouvel indice Legatum sur le Maroc
items.description: Le Maroc apparaît sous plusieurs facettes dans la nouvelle édition du Legatum Prosperity Index 2026. Au-delà des seuls indicateurs économiques, l’indice met en perspective le développement, les libertés et la solidité du tissu social, offrant ainsi une lecture plus large de la trajectoire du Royaume. Le Maroc occupe la 76e place sur les 161 pays couverts par l’édition 2026 du Legatum Prosperity Index. Le Royaume se situe ainsi devant plusieurs pays de son environnement régional, dont l’Algérie, classée 83e, et l’Égypte, 120e. La Tunisie conserve pour sa part une légère avance, au 75e rang. Cette position doit surtout être lue à la lumière de la nouvelle architecture de l’indice. Pour son édition 2026, le Legatum Institute a réorganisé son approche autour de trois grands domaines : le développement, les libertés et la société. L’objectif est de mesurer la prospérité à travers un ensemble de facteurs qui dépassent largement la seule richesse produite par une économie. Un Maroc en transformation économique Le profil consacré au Royaume dessine d’abord l’image d’une économie en phase d’industrialisation. Le Legatum Institute souligne la diversification progressive de ses activités et cite notamment les engrais, les phosphates, l’automobile et les agrumes parmi ses principales exportations. Cette évolution est importante dans la lecture de l’indice. Elle traduit le passage progressif d’une économie historiquement davantage centrée sur l’agriculture et certaines ressources naturelles vers un appareil productif plus diversifié, capable de s’insérer dans plusieurs chaînes de valeur internationales. Le profil du Maroc relève également l’importance de ses échanges avec l’extérieur. Aux côtés des produits industriels et agricoles exportés, le Royaume importe notamment des produits énergétiques, du blé et des équipements industriels. Cette structure reflète à la fois l’ouverture de l’économie et les besoins liés à son développement. Développement, libertés et société L’édition 2026 cherche à apprécier simultanément trois dimensions considérées comme complémentaires. Le domaine du développement s’intéresse aux conditions économiques et sociales qui permettent à une population d’améliorer durablement son niveau de vie. Le domaine des libertés examine, de son côté, les conditions dans lesquelles les individus peuvent exercer leurs droits et participer à la vie de leur société. Le troisième volet, consacré à la société, s’attache à la solidité des liens et des structures qui permettent à une communauté de fonctionner et de progresser. Cette approche offre une lecture plus complète du Maroc. Elle permet notamment de replacer les transformations économiques du Royaume dans un cadre plus large, où le développement humain, les conditions de vie et la cohésion sociale participent également à la construction de la prospérité. Le choix du Legatum Institute est d’autant plus intéressant que l’institut a revu sa méthodologie pour cette édition. Les données utilisées sont issues de nombreuses sources internationales et couvrent plusieurs années. Le classement précise également que sa méthodologie est réexaminée chaque année, ce qui signifie que les positions doivent être interprétées en tenant compte des évolutions apportées au mode de calcul. Pour le Maroc, cette nouvelle grille permet donc de regarder au-delà d’un simple rang. Sa 76e position mondiale constitue un repère, mais l’intérêt du profil réside surtout dans la manière dont le Royaume se situe sur les différentes composantes de la prospérité. Une position qui s’inscrit dans une dynamique plus large Le profil du Legatum Institute montre d’ailleurs que le Maroc reste proche de sa meilleure performance historique dans cet indice. Le Royaume a atteint son meilleur rang, 75e, tandis que son niveau le plus bas a été enregistré à la 80e place. Sa position actuelle de 76e le place donc à seulement une place de son meilleur classement historique. Cette donnée permet de relativiser une lecture strictement arithmétique du classement. Le Maroc n’est pas confronté à une rupture dans sa trajectoire au sein de l’indice : sa position actuelle reste proche de son meilleur niveau observé depuis la création de la série disponible pour le pays. Elle témoigne aussi d’une présence désormais bien installée du Royaume dans les comparaisons internationales portant sur la prospérité. Le Maroc devance notamment plusieurs économies émergentes et conserve une position supérieure à celle de plusieurs pays de sa région. À l’échelle mondiale, le classement reste dominé par des pays européens disposant de niveaux élevés de développement et de bien-être. La Suisse arrive en tête de l’édition 2026, devant la Norvège. La Finlande se classe 5e, l’Islande 6e et la Suède 7e, tandis que le Danemark occupe la 4e place. Le top 10 est ainsi dominé par les pays qui obtiennent les meilleurs résultats dans l’approche multidimensionnelle retenue par le Legatum. Pour le Maroc, le 76e rang sur 161 s’inscrit dans une trajectoire qui reste proche de son meilleur niveau historique, alors que le Royaume poursuit sa transformation économique et son développement sur plusieurs fronts. items.title: Osun election: APC’s founding chair, Bisi Akande wins polling unit
items.description: Former Osun State Governor and founding interim national chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Bisi Akande, has won his polling unit for the party’s governorship candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, in Saturday’s governorship election. Akande cast his ballot earlier in the day at Polling Unit 12, Ward 4, Atogbade area of Ila-Orangun, Ila Local Government Area. Oyebamiji secured 181 votes at the polling unit, defeating Accord Party candidate and incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, who polled 121 votes. Akande governed Osun State from 1999 to 2003 under the Alliance for Democracy (AD). After leaving office, he served as national chairman of the AD, Action Congress (AC) and Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) for 11 years between 2003 and 2014. He later became the founding interim national chairman of the APC following the formation of the party. items.title: NPP rebuilding to reclaim parliamentary seats lost in 2024 – Annoh-Dompreh
items.description: The Minority Chief Whip, Frank Annoh-Dompreh, says that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has begun efforts to rebuild its structures and regain parliamentary seats it lost to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2024 general elections. The Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP said the party had acknowledged the challenges that contributed to its poor electoral performance and was taking steps to address them ahead of the 2028 elections. Speaking to the media after casting his ballot during the NPP’s Eastern Regional elections on Saturday, August 15, Mr Annoh-Dompreh said the party was determined to learn from the setbacks it suffered in 2024. He said the NPP’s difficulties were not confined to individual constituencies, arguing that the party also lost ground in several constituencies it had traditionally considered strongholds. According to him, constituencies in the Western Region, Greater Accra and other parts of the country that had previously been considered safe for the NPP also proved challenging during the last election. “Myself I struggled and it is not just me. Nationally we struggled with even traditional seats; Takoradi, Awutu Senya and the many seats in Greater Accra that we win with ease, we struggled” he told Channel One TV. Mr Annoh-Dompreh said the party had accepted responsibility for its performance and was using the experience to prepare for the next election. He cautioned the governing NDC against assuming that the outcome of the 2024 election would automatically be repeated in 2028. “What the NDC should know is that every election comes with its own unique challenges and we have accepted that we had a unique challenge and we are ready to go over this challenge.” The Minority Chief Whip said the NPP had already begun laying the groundwork to strengthen its electoral fortunes, including rebuilding its grassroots structures and positioning itself to win back lost constituencies. He said the party’s focus was now on addressing the weaknesses exposed by the 2024 election and ensuring that its parliamentary candidates and constituency structures were better prepared for the 2028 polls. Mr Annoh-Dompreh expressed confidence that with the necessary groundwork, the NPP could recover the parliamentary seats it lost and improve its performance in the next general election.

items.title: Amorim’s AC Milan come from behind to beat Man United 4-2 as Chukwueze shines
items.description: Man United suffered a disappointing 4-2 defeat to AC Milan in Poland as Ruben Amorim’s side surrendered the lead twice before the Italian giants completed a second-half comeback. The result made for a difficult meeting between United and their former manager Amorim, who is now in charge of Milan. United made a flying start when Harry Maguire opened the scoring in the second minute, heading home from Bruno Fernandes’ corner. Amad Diallo almost doubled the advantage shortly afterwards, but Milan gradually grew into the contest. United goalkeeper Senne Lammens produced an important save to deny Ruben Loftus-Cheek before Milan eventually found an equaliser in the 37th minute. Goncalo Ramos created the opening for Samuel Chukwueze, who finished from close range to make it 1-1. United had an opportunity to restore their lead before half-time when they were awarded a penalty, but Fernandes saw his effort saved. Patrick Dorgu put United back in front six minutes after the restart after taking advantage of a poor back-pass from Filippo Terracciano. However, Milan responded quickly again. Alphadjo Cisse levelled in the 57th minute after Chukwueze created problems down the right and delivered for his teammate to score at the far post. Chukwueze was at the heart of Milan’s comeback once again four minutes later, setting up Ramos to head the visitors in front for the first time. Milan then exposed United’s right side again, with Loftus-Cheek racing through before making it 4-2 in the 71st minute. United’s attempts to change the game through their substitutes failed to produce a response as Milan held on for an impressive comeback victory. The match also provided an opportunity for several United players to return to action. Lisandro Martinez was gradually reintroduced following his World Cup involvement, while Kobbie Mainoo also made his return. Marcus Rashford came off the bench to make his first appearance for Manchester United in 20 months. With the new Premier League season approaching, United will have plenty to assess after allowing Milan to overturn a two-goal advantage and expose weaknesses at the back. items.title: IGE : 600 millions d’ouguiyas versés pour des travaux routiers qui n’ont pas été réalisés
items.description: L'Inspection générale de l'État a indiqué que 632 millions d'ouguiyas avaient été versés pour des travaux secondaires ou partiels qui n'avaient pas été réalisés, ou qui n'étaient pas conformes aux normes techniques prévues dans les contrats, ce qui constitue l'une des plus importantes irrégularités financières qu'elle ait constatées au cours de ses missions d'inspection. Cette information figure dans son rapport annuel sur les activités des années 2024 et 2025, qui a recensé des irrégularités financières et administratives dont l’impact total s’élève à environ 2,37 milliards d’ouguiyas. L’Inspection a précisé que ce type d’irrégularités est à l’origine des déficits les plus importants en termes d’impact financier, puisqu’il représente environ 27 % du total des pertes constatées, tandis que la deuxième cause en importance concerne des montants s’élevant à environ 478 millions d’ouguiyas, résultant du non-prélèvement et du non-recouvrement des pénalités de retard dues. Le rapport a également fait état d’une surfacturation de plus de 170 millions d’ouguiyas, d’un manque à gagner de plus de 165 millions d’ouguiyas sur les sommes dues à l’État, ainsi que d’un défaut de prélèvement et de versement d’impôts s’élevant à plus de 163 millions d’ouguiyas, ce qui constitue l’un des principaux postes ayant contribué à la hausse de l’impact financier total des irrégularités. L’Inspection a également constaté le dépôt de fonds publics dans des établissements financiers en difficulté pour un montant avoisinant les 116 millions d’ouguiyas, ainsi que des dépenses sans contrepartie s’élevant à plus de 86 millions d’ouguiyas, ainsi que des dépenses non étayées par des pièces justificatives suffisantes pour un montant supérieur à 82 millions, sans compter l’octroi d’avantages indus à des fonctionnaires pour un montant de plus de 77 millions d’ouguiyas. Les irrégularités comprenaient également la réduction ou l’exonération injustifiée de recettes dues à l’État, des lacunes dans le recouvrement des recettes, le détournement de fonds, des dépenses injustifiées, le non-paiement des droits d’enregistrement des contrats, ainsi que le versement de sommes pour du matériel et des équipements non livrés. Sur le plan administratif, le rapport a relevé des irrégularités dont l’impact financier direct n’a pas été établi, mais qui ont affecté les procédures de contrôle, les transactions et la gestion. En tête de liste figurent les lacunes du système de contrôle interne (16 cas), suivies de la concurrence fictive (12 cas), puis des accords directs non justifiés et du non-respect des seuils de compétence (10 cas). Le rapport a également recensé neuf cas de souscription manquant de transparence et de fractionnement des dépenses, et sept cas d’installations, d’équipements et d’études non utilisés, ainsi que des irrégularités concernant la planification des transactions, le versement d’avances aux fournisseurs en violation des procédures, l’abus d’influence et l’abus de fonction, la collusion dans les transactions, la falsification de documents administratifs et les conflits d’intérêts.

items.title: ‘They’ll go a second time, a third, a fourth’: The battlefield Wadi al-Mollak’s farm laborers can’t but return to
items.description: In the daily battle to put bread on the table, buy cooking gas, pay for education and healthcare, the daily battle to provide for the basic necessities of life, the farm laborers of the Wadi al-Mollak village in Sharqiya fight without land, schools, hospitals, roads or transportation fit for humans, without drinking water or a sanitation system, without work that can guarantee subsistence, let alo ne a “Hayah Karima.” And yet everyone fights. Men, youth and children are packed every day by the dozens into the dabbaba (tank), as the open-bed pickup truck is known. They set off at the first light of dawn along a deadly road they have no choice but to take. They head to the large farms within the village or in Ismailia, to earn enough to get by and keep fighting. That is why when their sons come back from the battlefield as lifeless bodies, instead of bringing home the little they had gone out to earn, the tragedy is more than the loss of loved ones. It is an utter defeat that can take years to overcome. So we saw it on our visit to Ezbet al-Dawoudiya, one of dozens of similar ezbas in Wadi al-Mollak. We arrived on Thursday. Two days earlier, a dabbaba carrying some of Dawoudiya’s residents to work at mango farms belonging to the Armed Forces’ National Service Projects Organizations in the Abu Sultan area of Ismailia collided with another coming from the opposite direction from the Bahr al-Baqar village, carrying boys and girls to other farms in the same area. The collision killed 19 people , including one person from Dawoudiya whom the residents tell us succumbed to his injuries on Saturday. Twenty nine more people were injured in the crash. In total, 12 of the village’s young men and children were killed and six others injured, some critically. *** “We want to go to the funeral,” we tell the driver of the dabbaba, the only way to get to the ezbas of the village. “Which funeral?” he asks. “The one in Abu Ghazbawy, Abu Agwa or Shelh? There’s one or two dead in each. The group funeral was Wednesday. The governor came and all the big shots.” Following the advice of the women sitting beside us in the truck, we decide to go to Dawoudiya, the ezba with the largest number of victims: eight killed and six injured, residents would tell us later. The truck sets off along a partly paved road no more than four meters wide, running between two canals. There were no street lights. Every time we hit a bump or a pothole, we grip the truck’s metal rails tighter. Day laborers in Wadi al-Mollak do not only work in the mango harvest during the summer. Throughout the year, they also pick fruit in the large citrus farms surrounding them, or they sort and pack produce at export stations in Beheira and Alexandria, village residents will tell us later. The workers are taken to those farms and stations in the same open pick-ups they use to reach the mango farms. Most of the land in Wadi al-Mollak once belonged to Arabia for Land Reclamation , established in the 1960s. The farm laborers called it the “Yugoslav company” because it brought in experts and equipment for desert land reclamation from Yugoslavia. “When I was young, I used to work as a day laborer for the company. I would earn a quarter of a pound,” a man in his seventies from Mollak recalls. “Then, in the 1990s, we woke up one day to find out they had sold large areas of the land to businessmen. We don’t know how. And we’re the people who live here, we didn’t even get a single qirat (175 square meters) of the land.” On our way to Dawoudiya, we listen to the women’s grievances, which pour out after they learn we are on a reporting assignment. They first lament “the youth who die just to earn their daily bread,” then the rising prices and lack of services. They point to the road, which they say has remained in the same condition for years. As crashes kept happening there, residents have repeatedly requested it be finished and one of the canals be covered to widen it. But their calls went unheeded until Wednesday, when the local administrative unit added a layer of sand to the road to make it easier for the high-end cars carrying officials to reach the site of the group funeral. The women stop talking only to point out the funeral sites along both sides of the road, each one as we pass it. “Here, there was a funeral. Two died. And here, there was another funeral. One or two died. So-and-so’s sons.” When we reach Dawoudiya, a coffin is waiting for us at the entrance to the ezba. It has not yet been returned to the mosque after the funeral procession. Next, we reach a group of young men, their faces heavy with exhaustion. One of them leads us to the funeral gathering for Ahmed and Youssef, the sons of Abdel Karim Selim, an agricultural day laborer. Ahmed had received his thanaweya amma certificate this year and was waiting for his university placement results to find out whether he would be admitted to the faculty of commerce, his father tells us. He had decided to work during the summer break to help cover some of the university costs, so he accepted a contractor’s offer to pick mangoes in Abu Sultan. Youssef, 16, was already used to working even while he was in school, earning LE150 or LE200 a day to help his family cover their living expenses, the father says. His studies for a commercial diploma did not require him to attend school regularly. Tears overcome Selim, and he falls silent. Another at the funeral gathering explains that the father now only has 14-year-old Ibrahim. He will look after Ibrahim on his own — the boys’ mother died some time ago. Next to Selim sits his younger brother, Adel, also a day laborer. His eldest son, 19, was badly injured in the accident and is in the intensive care unit. “He used to help me with living expenses. I applied for the Takaful and Karama pension three years ago, but my application was rejected even after I submitted all the papers proving I have nothing. But [the local Social Solidarity Ministry staff] told me, ‘You’re above the poverty line.’” Adel also applied at the labor directorate in Abu Hammad for the government grant for irregular workers. But staff told him that his employer should register him in order for him to be added to the grant list. “They even stopped food subsidies for a lot of people in the ezba. How are we supposed to live?” Adel says. Among the group is Ahmed, a middle-school student and the cousin of the two brothers who died. He escaped the crash by pure chance. He was supposed to ride in the same truck with around 20 others, but after getting into a fight with one of them, he took another truck instead. From there, he saw the moment when a tire on the first truck ahead of him blew out near Ismailia’s Dawawis area. It veered off course just as the Bahr al-Baqar truck came speeding toward it. In an instant, everyone aboard both vehicles was thrown into the air and hurled onto the asphalt. Ahmed recalls a mbulances arriving about half an hour later and taking the victims to the Qassasin Central Hospital in Ismailia. By evening, thousands of residents from Mollak and Bahr al-Baqar had gathered outside the hospital. As Central Security Forces vehicles surrounded the crowd, residents of Qassasin brought food and water and offered their condolences, according to another Dawoudiya resident who was present at the hospital. People at the funeral gathering rush to defend the truck driver, Am Sayyed, who is also the work contractor. They say he turned himself in to the police despite being injured. Prosecutors said they could not question him, the other driver or many of the injured “due to their medical condition.” The mourners blame the deteriorated state of the Dawawis road, which extends from the Molak village road. The Dawawis road is wider, about six meters, and while it is paved with asphalt, it is riddled with potholes and bumps. Vehicles travel in both directions along two narrow lanes separated by a painted white line, residents say. They point to repeated fatal accidents on the road, detailed by a report from the Center for Trade Union and Workers Services following the latest crash. When we ask Selim whether Ibrahim will go back to work on the farms, the people around him respond on his behalf, giving different answers. “No,” one of them says. “After what happened, none of our boys are going back.” Another man, who had previously worked as a labor contractor, disagrees. “They’ll go. I’m telling you, they’ll go,” he says. “Who sits around without work? You have to go to work to be a man. If he doesn’t go out to work, he’ll be up to no good. What if something happens to me tomorrow morning? Shouldn’t my son be a man, feed himself and stand by his father? Sorry, but we’re not going to be doctors. We have to have the boys get used to working, otherwise they’ll become lazy.” “No,” another of the funeral attendees stands up suddenly to shout. “They’ll go back a second time, a third, a fourth. Because if they don’t go, they won’t be able to feed themselves. Where are you going to get the LE350 for a gas cylinder from? That’s two days’ wages. And that loaf of bread that’s now for LE1.5 … and on and on.” He sits back down and lays his hand, which was raised trembling in anger, onto the ground where we are sitting in front of Selim’s house. “Do you know what we’re sitting on right now?” he asks us. “This is a sewage tank. It has to be emptied every 15 days, and it costs around LE1,000-1,500 to do so. That’s what the boys were working to pay for. And you tell me they’re not going back? Man, screw the …” He falls silent as though hesitating. He erupts again: “those pashas who came to the group funeral yesterday, the one the governorate spent a million pounds on, they arrived surrounded by guards so we couldn’t get near them. They laid sand over the ground and brought in a special kitchen to cook them meat, chicken and stew. And the people whose children died, who hadn’t eaten for two days, didn’t see a thing. But when it’s election time …” When we ask another of the attendees about the speake r’s anger he tells us in a whisper that when the speaker’s mother fell ill a few months ago, he was unable to get her to the nearest hospital at Abu Hammad, around 20 km from the village. “They refused to send an ambulance, saying the road is in too bad of a state. And the health unit in the village doesn’t provide service. In the end, she died. The situation is really difficult here.” Complaints about the lack of public services pour, one after another. There is the road connecting the ezbas, which has become narrower over time after the local administrative unit cut down the trees along its sides, leaving it exposed to erosion from the two canals. One resident brings up the frequent drinking water outages , especially during the summer months, as well as its poor quality. Beyond the drinking-water problems, which are common in different parts of rural Egypt, the village also has a layered problem with electricity. During the summer, power cuts lasting one to two hours have become part of the daily routine. When the electricity does come back, the current fluctuates, damaging appliances and sometimes causing fires, one resident says. “And if there’s a fire, there is no fire station here. By the time they come from [Abu Hammad], either the house will be gone, or we’ll have put it out ourselves,” another resident says. As for education, “65 ezbas, and there are only five primary schools and two middle schools. There is not a single general or technical secondary school. The nearest secondary school is in Abu Hammad,” says Atef Abdallah, another resident of Dawoudiya. “Imagine, school boys and girls getting up every morning, in the dead of cold weather, to get on the dabbaba to go to school. How is that acceptable to anyone?” After talking with the people outside Selim’s house, we head to the home of his neighbor, Mohamed Saeed. He lost his son Mostafa, 18, in the crash. His other two sons, Ahmed, 22, and Saeed, 20, are in the hospital being treated for serious injuries. The father is unable to speak to us. Our companion takes us instead to the neighboring house. “This is Haj Khaled Ahmed’s house. His son Mohamed, 24, had been married for a year. His wife is seven months pregnant. L’IGE au ministère de l’HUAT : des contrats fondés sur de fausses déclarations et des travaux non réalisés
items.description: L'Inspection générale de l'État a constaté des irrégularités dans la gestion du secteur de l’habitat et de l'urbanisme, notamment le versement de sommes pour des travaux non réalisés ou non conformes aux normes techniques, des doubles paiements sans contrepartie, du matériel non livré, ainsi que l'attribution de marchés sur la base de déclarations falsifiées, ainsi que le recours injustifié à des accords de gré à gré et au fractionnement des dépenses. L’Inspection générale de l’État a mené quatre missions de contrôle et d’enquête portant sur un secteur ministériel et trois établissements publics entre 2020 et 2023, pour un montant total de plus de 10,87 milliards d’ouguiyas. Selon le rapport annuel de l’Inspection générale de l’État, les travaux de contrôle ont mis en évidence un manque de transparence dans la mise en œuvre des conventions de délégation des marchés publics, ainsi que l’existence de pratiques parallèles de gestion financière échappant au système de contrôle interne des finances publiques. Des cas d’attribution de marchés publics sur la base de déclarations falsifiées, de recours injustifié à la négociation de gré à gré, de cession illégale de marchés et de fractionnement des dépenses ont également été constatés, ainsi que la facturation en double de certains travaux lors de la réattribution des marchés. Les inspections sur le terrain, menées avec la participation d’experts techniques, ont révélé des travaux secondaires ou partiels non réalisés et d’autres non conformes aux normes techniques, ainsi qu’une détérioration prématurée de certaines installations et la réalisation d’infrastructures coûteuses restées inutilisées. Le rapport a également relevé des cas de conflits d’intérêts liés au fait que des entrepreneurs se sont chargés de passer des contrats avec des bureaux de contrôle et des laboratoires d’essais de qualité, ainsi que des lacunes dans les mécanismes de contrôle technique, de suivi des travaux et de procédures de réception des ouvrages. Parmi les irrégularités ayant une incidence financière figuraient le versement de sommes pour des travaux non exécutés ou non conformes aux spécifications, des doubles paiements sans contrepartie, des montants versés pour des équipements non livrés, ainsi que la non-application et le non-recouvrement des pénalités de retard et l'octroi d'avantages indus. L’Inspection a également constaté que les avances sur le démarrage des travaux et les garanties de bonne exécution n’avaient pas été régularisées après l’interruption des travaux et le retrait des entrepreneurs, et que des sommes dues avaient été versées avant le paiement des droits d’enregistrement. Dans le domaine des marchés et de la gestion, le rapport a relevé des cas d’abus d’influence et d’abus de fonction, des pratiques collusoires visant à attribuer des marchés en dessous du seuil légal, la falsification de déclarations dans le but d’obtenir un avantage dans le cadre des marchés publics, ainsi que la non-récupération des excédents après l’exécution des conventions de délégation de travaux publics. Les irrégularités comprenaient également la conclusion de marchés de gré à gré sans disposer des crédits financiers nécessaires, le fractionnement des dépenses, la concurrence fictive, la cession illégale de marchés publics, ainsi que l’absence de contrôle technique, les lacunes dans le suivi de l’exécution des travaux et le non-respect des spécifications techniques.

items.title: Marruecos frustra el intento de cientos de migrantes subsaharianos de alcanzar Ceuta
items.description: Las fuerzas de seguridad de Marruecos han frustrado este sábado un intento de cruzar de forma irregular a la ciudad española de Ceuta de cientos de migrantes, en su mayoría subsaharianos, que se habían ocultado en las afueras de Castillejos, ciudad fronteriza con España. Cerca del mediodía, la policía de Marruecos ha cargado contra centenares de migrantes subsaharianos a las afueras de Castillejos. Han interceptado a 111 migrantes, en su mayoría subsaharianos, que intentaban alcanzar la frontera de Ceuta, y han detenido a 61 personas por incitar a la migración ilegal, según fuentes de seguridad marroquí citadas por Efe. El diario digital marroquí Hespress eleva a 249 la cifra de personas interceptadas que pretendían cruzar a España. La masa de subsaharianos se mantenía concentrada en una vaguada del barrio de Cerámica, el más cercano a la frontera; desde ahí, la policía marroquí los ha alejado forzosamente en autobuses fletados por las autoridades a diferentes partes del país, como a Uarzazate, a más de 800 kilómetros de la frontera con España. items.title: AJK elections: PPP, PML-N candidates retain lead in Bagh after repolling
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Sardar Ziaul Qamar of the PPP and Sardar Mir Akbar of the PML-N retained the lead in their respective constituencies in Bagh, after results were received from all 23 polling stations where repolling was held on Saturday. According to unofficial and unverified results, Qamar defeated the PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas in LA-15 (Central Bagh) by 1,891 votes. He secured 17,118 votes against Minhas’s 15,227. Repolling was held at nine polling stations in the constituency. It was the third consecutive defeat for Minhas in the constituency, who had entered electoral politics in 2016 under the banner of the PML-N, won that election and served as a minister during the following five years. Qamar, meanwhile, secured his second consecutive victory after winning the 2023 by-election. In LA-16 (Eastern Bagh), the PML-N’s Akbar defeated the PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman by 3,833 votes, securing 20,796 votes against his rival’s 16,963. Repolling was held at 14 polling stations in the constituency. Akbar has won four elections previously, making Saturday’s victory his fifth overall and third consecutive win. According to local journalists, Akbar’s sustained presence in his constituency, where he regularly attends celebrations, is believed to have contributed to his popularity. Constituents said he was known for attending even occasions marking the death of villagers’ livestock. Turnout remained low in both constituencies, according to witnesses, with voters at some polling stations “voluntarily” opting not to cast their ballots. Polling was, however, held peacefully, with adequate security arrangements for polling staff and voters. Polling officials described the conduct of voters towards them and security personnel as cordial. “Though no voters showed up [at some polling stations], the attitude and cooperation of local notables with polling staff and security forces was exemplary, including arrangements for their accommodation and meals,” said a presiding officer in LA-15. The repolling results took the PML-N’s tally to 25 seats and the PPP’s to 12 in the AJK Legislative Assembly. Sajid Iqbal Abbasi, who won LA-14 (Dhirkot) against Muslim Conference president and former AJK premier Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan by a large margin, also reportedly decided to support the PML-N. Monday results In the third phase of polling on Monday, PPP’s Qamar secured 16,637 votes in LA-15 (Bagh Central), followed by PML-N’s Minhas with 15,015 and Jamaat-i-Islami’s retired Brig Dr Muhammad Khan with 12,259. But as polling could not be held at nine stations in the constituency, the commission withheld the result. Similarly, the result of LA-16 (Eastern Bagh) was also withheld after polling could not be held at 14 stations, which have a combined 7,238 registered voters. Results from the remaining polling stations showed that PML-N’s Akbar, who secured 19,515 votes, was leading his closest rival, PPP’s Zaman, by 3,225 votes. In both constituencies, all five candidates had accused their opponents of rigging. Rathore notified as returned candidate from LA-17 Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission notified AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore as the returned candidate from LA-17. The notification was issued late on Friday and was provided to the media on Saturday. LA-17 (Haveli), where Rathore was contesting from, emerged as the most contentious constituency during the third phase of the polls on Monday. The election was thrown into fresh controversy on Wednesday after the returning officer issued the Form 27 declaring him the winner despite an assurance, according to his PML-N rival Engr Mohsin Aziz, that the result would not be announced until his complaint was taken up by the Election Commission. Aziz subsequently challenged the election, with the AJK Chief Election Co­­mmissioner (CEC) retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Thursday reserving his decision after hearing arguments from both sides. On Saturday, the Election Commission said that it would announce the verdict on the petitions at 5pm. AJK polls The PML-N bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur division in the first phase on July 27 and 15 in the second phase on Aug 2 comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The PPP, on the other hand, won only 10 constituencies during these phases. The polls are being held in phases amid unrest in the region. The third phase, held on Monday, was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. On Monday, polls went ahead in Bagh and Haveli, but the Election Commission later withheld the results of two constituencies pending repolling at 23 polling stations. It announced the result for LA-14 (Bagh-I), commonly known as Dhirkot, where Jammu Kashmir Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sajid Iqbal Abbasi secured a landslide victory with 40,522 votes.

items.title: Yemen's Mocha port halts operations after Houthi attacks, port director says
items.description: Aug 15 (Reuters) - Yemen's Mocha port has suspended commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's director said on Saturday.
